summary: Tenant routed to secondary variant despite explicit model pin during orchestrator retry surge
description: Issue summary: One enterprise customer observed tenant traffic being routed to a secondary (fallback) variant even though their project had an explicit model version pin. Impact: customer-facing production traffic experienced degraded model behavior and increased cost due to falling back to a larger, higher-cost variant. This started during a rolling canary of a separate release when orchestrator retry activity spiked.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a tenant-level model pin to redwood/rlhf-3b-v2 with strict affinity; 2) Initiate a rolling canary that toggles health checks for a different model in the same region to induce orchestrator retries; 3) Observe routing decisions in the control plane and edge traces for a burst window; 4) Repeat with increased orchestrator retry rate and note whether pinned affinity holds.
observed_behavior: During a control-plane retry surge the tenant's session affinity was dropped and requests were routed to the secondary variant for ~8 minutes. Edge traces show the pin still present in the tenant metadata but the orchestrator returned a fallback routing decision. Requests received mixed variant outputs and embeddings were inconsistent with pinned model behavior.
expected_behavior: Tenant-level explicit pins should be honored across transient orchestrator retries; traffic must remain bound to pinned model unless an explicit unpin or capacity-driven fallback policy is triggered by SLOs.
logs:

Relevant trace IDs: trace-4a7b2d, trace-4a7b91. Full logs attached in internal archive (link in comments).
investigation_notes: Initial triage by support: verified tenant pin exists and was set before the window. SRE pulled orchestrator commit logs and found that a retry sequence with duplicate commit_nonce values and a race in the grace-window update caused the grace_window_reset flag to be set erroneously. Hypothesis: orchestrator retry path treats a repeated commit attempt that includes a non-zero retry counter as a new commit for epoch reconciliation, which resets the pin's grace timer and allows fallback evaluation. Reproduced in staging by forcing commit_retry > 2 and toggling health probes. Engineering lead (J. Patel) identified a conditional in orchestrator/commit_manager that fails to short-circuit for duplicate commit_id when retry_count > 0 (see related PR).
mitigation_steps:
- Short term: Set customer routing policy to strict-pin on the tenant to stop further fallback decisions (applied at 2025-02-13T15:05Z).
- Throttle canary healthcheck toggles to reduce orchestrator retry storms while patch is prepared.
- Coordinate with Customer Success to notify Acme AI and confirm mitigation.
resolution_notes: Engineering pushed hotfix v2025.02.14-orch.1 to orchestrator in eu-west on 2025-02-14 04:30 UTC which adjusts commit_manager to ignore duplicate commit_id when retry_count > 0 and preserves existing grace_window unless an explicit unpin event occurs. Post-deploy monitoring shows pin stability restored; no additional fallback routing observed for the tenant in the 72-hour window after patch. A follow-up stabilization release scheduled to fully harden edge-proxy interaction.
